comments.note: CONFIRMED: handleListKnowledge intentionally uses InsightScope.safeParse() (silent ignore). The docstring on line 169 of api-knowledge.ts explicitly documents: '`scope` is validated via `InsightScope.safeParse()`; unrecognised values are silently treated as no scope filter rather than causing an error.' This is a documented deliberate design decision consistent with the handler's lenient query-parameter style — the pattern mirrors how invalid limit/offset values are silently coerced to defaults. The test at line 767 correctly asserts on this behaviour. No action needed.

CONFIRMED: The 5 api-client.test.ts failures are pre-existing and out-of-scope for WP-010. api-client.js was migrated project_slug → repository_name in WP-008 (commit 3ede3e3) but the test file was never updated. WP-010 did not touch api-client.test.ts. Acknowledged as a known backlog item. No action in this WP.

Fix-Forward: The module-level JSDoc block comment (lines 1-27) refers to 'WP-009' in the title and storage-layer case counts. The test file is for WP-010 per the ledger (the WP-009.md file naming is a pre-existing ledger quirk). The comment counts also list '16 cases' but the file has 17 storage-layer tests and 14 handler tests (not 10), making the count inaccurate. Updated the header comment to 'WP-010' and corrected the storage/handler case counts to match the actual file content (17 storage-layer, 14 handler-layer). No behavioural change.

[documentation-forward] The known-limitation block in api-knowledge.ts (lines 17-30) correctly documents that handleDeleteKnowledge and handlePromoteKnowledge accept repository_name as a raw string without PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX validation at the handler level, returning HTTP 500 rather than HTTP 400 for malformed slugs. This is currently only in the source file JSDoc. A public API reference doc or README should surface this limitation and the remediation path (adding explicit Zod guard mirroring handleMoveKnowledge/handleUpdateKnowledge) so future contributors can action it without reading implementation code.

Minor: The identity-move test at line 428-437 (storage layer) uses a hardcoded ID 1 without seeding data. This is correct — the identity-guard in moveInsight() fires before any store lookup — but the test string toThrow() with no argument means any thrown error passes. It would be more precise to assert on the specific error message fragment ('Cannot move insight to the same repository store') to prevent false positives if the error source changes. Low priority, does not block PASS.
